title: Cantilever column with axial load and a small lateral load: second-order moment and deflection

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: AISC, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings, 2005, p. 16.1-435, Case 2 (the 2005 edition was not opened; the same benchmark of the 2022 edition is in ../aisc-commentary) - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Cantilever column of 300 in, built in at the base, free at the top; W8x18 with the moment of inertia the page gives, Iz = 61.9 in^4, E = 29,000 ksi; axial load 30 kip and lateral load 0.09 kip at the top. Combination 'second': second-order analysis of both loads (the engine's member carries the exact stability functions); combination 'first': first-order analysis of the lateral load alone. The area does not enter the targets (placeholder 10 in^2); Iy = 1000 Iz so that no out-of-plane buckling enters. The lateral load is 0.003 x 30 kip = 0.09 kip (the page's text has '0.03 x 30'; its arithmetic uses 0.09). The page's closed form uses the full E (no stiffness reduction).  Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.
